text:
deploy-bot: Automated: Rollout paused for release v2026.03.18-rc4 in eu-west-1 due to elevated 401 rates from authz-service. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-4821 :warning:
olivia: Noted. Which canaries are currently in-flight?
raj: Canary group A (eu-west-1) is paused at 3/3. Observed: authz 401 spike +15% since 08:12 UTC.
oncall-dan: I'm on it — just got paged. Initial triage suggests token introspection failing on a subset of hosts. Investigating token cache layer now, ETA ~20-30m.
maria: If this lingers >30m we should prepare rollback plan. Need to avoid a noisy failover.
olivia: Agreed. Rollback target would be v2026.03.17-hotfix which is backward compatible. Any blockers for a staged rollback?
raj: We could also pin traffic to the stable pool rather than rolling back globally. Pin = safer, avoids DB migrations. But depends on routing control.
oncall-dan: Ops note: I can perform a staged rollback if needed. Command I will run (if agreed):
```
deploy rollback --to v2026.03.17-hotfix --env=eu-west-1 --staged --wait
```
Prefer to try routing pin first.
maria: I'll prepare the calendar update and a short customer-facing note explaining the hold (AuthZ outage). Who will draft the release-note blurb?
olivia: Maria can draft. Also post a brief ticket update in the release tracker and flag the change window if we end up rescheduling.
maria: Draft blurb: "Release paused due to third-party AuthZ instability causing elevated 401 rates; rescheduling tentative window if unresolved. No schema or data changes. Rollback safe to v2026.03.17-hotfix." Paste to GH after confirmation.
raj: If we pin, I'll push config patch to pin=2026.03.17-hotfix for eu-west-1 and run smoke once routing changes land.
oncall-dan: Triage update: AuthZ team applied a token-cache patch to a subset of hosts; telemetry looks promising but still early. If rates don't stabilize in 45m, propose moving release to Tomorrow 09:00 UTC and run rollback plan. Who owns schedule change?
maria: I'll update calendar and open a reschedule PR in the release repo. Will also add the reason to the changelog.
olivia: Also add a note in #customers-notices? Small FYI: "Minor hold on rolling release in EU due to downstream auth service; no user data changes."
maria: Done — calendar hold + changelog PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/release-notes/pull/432
raj: Pre-rollback checklist if needed: snapshot canary metrics, backup routing config, prepare rollback command, notify on-call. I'll queue smoke tests:
```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://internal.redwood/eu-west/health || echo FAIL
```
olivia: Good. Keep the release ticket status: "on hold - incident" and add ops owner.
oncall-dan: Update: AuthZ team reports their patch landed across all hosts at 08:35 UTC. Monitoring: 401s dropping toward baseline over last 5m. I'm seeing token-introspect latency normalize. Standby to resume.
deploy-bot: Notice: Rollout remains paused per previous command. Awaiting SRE sign-off to resume or operator-triggered rollback.
oncall-dan: SRE sign-off: authz looks stable, I'll resume canary in 2m and watch for regressions.
deploy-bot: Command executed: resume rollout for v2026.03.18-rc4 in eu-west-1. Progress: 1/3 -> 2/3 -> 3/3.
raj: Smoke tests pass, health endpoints 200, no spike in 5xx or latency.
olivia: Great. No reschedule needed. Maria, can you close calendar hold and mark reschedule draft as cancelled but keep changelog PR for transparency?
maria: Done. Calendar hold cleared; reschedule PR closed (marked as cancelled). Changelog PR left open for audit.
oliivia: Thanks team — please add any post-mortem notes to the incident doc if anything else pops up.
deploy-bot: Thread: rollout resumed and completed for v2026.03.18-rc4. Closed at ts 2732105944.
